text: Started with restored and live logs across all three hosts; checking successful access, application events and scheduled-job trust boundaries against staff/service baselines. A restart or internet probes alone are not compromise.

Removed undocumented jpark account access and sudo membership (not on owner-approved directory; no successful logins in restored logs), revoked unrestricted deploy sudo rsync while retaining the fixed CI release command, and initiated signed internal mirror refresh for Grafana.

Disabled obsolete unauthenticated WordPress support endpoint (config disclosure and cache modification). Nginx now blocks source backups, hidden files and PHP in uploads/cache before the PHP handler; ordinary image and page routes remain available.

Root dashboard no longer runs WordPress PHP or evaluates DB-derived shell assignments; it uses the root-owned client config. Removed root recursive chown from the release. Mailing exports now create CSVs as the requesting user; root never writes to paths in a staff home.

CI maintenance now runs only local verified scripts; Git maintenance runs as deploy, not root, against the staff-writable repository. CI release no longer has an agent-forwarding path. Removed the unused reverse login key on CI, which was the same private identity used to publish to web.
Coordinating CI backup key lockdown to an uploads-only restricted rsync receiver. Both normal and nightly send to the same archival folder through its new restricted root.
Backup identity is now source-bound and upload-only into the archive folder using rrsync, with its trust file controlled by root.
Enabled MariaDB connection and table audit metadata with bounded local rotation; it does not capture statements or secret values.

Restricted the web CI key to ci-01 and disabled deploy forwarding. Password access remains narrowly available for the recorded old monitor, Maria, and office during migration; human SSH accounts are unchanged. Root owns non-deployed WordPress code and the internal maintenance mirror; uploads and deployment destinations retain their operational owners.

Kept authenticated Grafana reachable for roaming staff and rejected the vulnerable 8.3.0 package in apt; live 8.3.1 failed the scanner traversal probe. Restricted unauthenticated node metrics to the office network/loopback.

Scoped database TCP to web-01 and localhost; SSH and local database use remain unchanged. Dump creation now fails on mysqldump errors instead of publishing a successful gzip of a failed dump, and uses private permissions.

Restricted the Git remote configuration (shared token) to root and the existing authorized developer group and made offsite credentials root-only. Both staff git reads and scheduled releases remain healthy.
Captured invoice amount/status baseline in a root-only evidence directory to compare against reviewed bookkeeper activity and the upcoming batch.

The off-directory Unix contractor also had a legacy WordPress administrator account, registered at the original site setup with no observed current access. Removed the role, destroyed sessions and disabled the known old password while retaining content attribution.

No newer Forminator artifact is available on the mirror. Added independent pre-upload validation by filename extension and detected photo MIME for public uploads, alongside the existing no-PHP upload routes; disabled per-folder PHP settings and restricted FPM to .php.
Verified a scheduled encrypted dump was delivered to CI; local decryption and tar inventory contain both current DB dumps. Source and received archive checksums match.
Enabled Grafana access logging for successful and failed requests, retaining port 3000 for legitimate remote staff. Verified the service restarted on the patched version.

Removed payment bearer, storage auth and Redis password exposure through job process arguments. Confirmed read-only settlement and storage-gateway manifest check; will verify the scheduled 17:14 payout rather than triggering a duplicate batch.

Limited POST login/XML-RPC attempts per source without affecting normal visits or occasional staff logins; confirmed site, login page, sitemap, ride-story form, rental availability API and billing payout check.

A listed marketing user tried a sudo read of payment settings; sudo explicitly denied it. The matching historical SSH key and ordinary later mailing exports do not establish stolen credentials or a successful secret read. Monitoring that distinction.

Confirmed at 17:13:44 the marketing account exported all 240 customer records using the support-only ID lookup from 172.56.158.70. Same iPad credential previously tried reading payment settings via sudo and was denied. Preserved and removed bulk export, removed that session credential only, and enforced export roles and a small lookup cap while keeping ordinary approved marketing access.

Matched the bookkeeper’s legitimate correction to the authoritative order total; no anomalous DB login, invoice or payout identified. Added order-amount validation and stripped the web billing user of blanket schema writes while preserving payout reconciliation, marketing/support reads, and provider-key rotation.

DB audit independently confirms the marketing export session was a customers SELECT through the existing web DB user, not a database login by the remote device. The scheduled 17:14 payout sent 10, and the only later invoice edit matched the authoritative order.

CI has no matching remote source or unexpected login. Scheduled release and local maintenance are healthy. The CI-to-Wasabi full offsite check already failed before the shift (no external route); local encrypted archive delivery is verified.

Marketing shell history records a command to print the customer CSV, so treat it as likely displayed on the remote client. No evidence of further transfer or other host access; retained only the confirmed device revocation and left normal marketing/support workflows open.
